audit.whatIsWrong: The level chart labels levels 2, 3 and 4-5 as 'Skill' while the content whys for those same rows say Mel clearly owns them, and the 2+ item row is labelled 'Skill' while its why calls Sylas a teamfight flex.
audit.why: Sylas is a 400-range melee mage into a 950/1000-range mage with Rebuttal on top; Mel genuinely owns levels 2 through 5. Sylas's 58.02% winrate comes from level 6 onward, which is what the packet chart also shows.
audit.corrected: Rows 2/3/4-5 to Mel, row 2+ items to Sylas, with matching phases[].side and win[] pairs and why text rewritten to agree.

audit.why: Level 3 full kit, level 6 Hijack, Riftmaker and 2+ items are the right four doors; only the first-item why needed to stop handing the spike to Mel when the full layer already gives it to Sylas.
audit.corrected: whys[5] rewritten to Sylas's Riftmaker timing so both layers agree on the first-item row.

audit.whatIsWrong: Text repeatedly credits Sylas's E2 with a stun ('no stun', 'one clean E2 stun'), and claims Mel's ultimate reflects projectiles. Rebuttal is also described as a 'fifteen-second' window.
audit.why: Abduct (E2) pulls Sylas to a target and deals damage; it does not stun — the mirror audit states the same. The reflect is Rebuttal (W), not Golden Eclipse (R); Golden Eclipse strikes every Overwhelm-marked enemy at 25000 range. Rebuttal's cooldown is 38/35/33/29/26s, not fifteen.
audit.corrected: Stun claims removed, reflect attributed to Rebuttal only, Golden Eclipse described as the global Overwhelm detonation, real Rebuttal cooldown used.

audit.whatIsWrong: Nothing warns about Searing Brilliance — Mel's post-cast attack carries up to nine bonus projectiles and is the burst tell.
audit.why: The missingInteractions entry for this matchup flags the auto-reset burst tell; the wind-up, not the ability cast, is the cue to disengage.

edits.before: Get on him with E2 the moment Rebuttal is down — one full chain with the W heal erases a poke deficit.
edits.after: Get on her the instant Rebuttal ends — a 26-38s cooldown; one E2 chain with the W heal erases her poke lead.

edits.before: Engaging with both E charges spent — no shield, no stun, and you're a melee mage standing in the open.
edits.after: Engaging with both E charges spent — Abduct is your only gap-close, and without it a melee mage has no exit.

edits.before: Mel burns Rebuttal on nothing — take the fifteen-second invitation.
edits.after: Mel burns Rebuttal on nothing — that is a 26-38 second window.

edits.before: That is Mel’s whole plan in one window — decline politely and watch it retire.
edits.after: Her bonus-projectile attack after any cast is the tell — step back on the wind-up.

edits.before: Engaging with both E charges spent — no shield, no stun, and you're a melee mage standing in the open.
edits.after: Overwhelm stacks execute you later, so spend the stolen R in the fight that stacked them, not the next one.

edits.before: W online — the burst-heal turns even trades into wins. Take the extended trade only when his answer is down.
edits.after: Kingslayer heals, but Radiant Volley outranges everything you own — she chips from 950 and you cannot answer yet.

edits.before: Full kit: E2 chain into Q-W-AA is a real chunk, and E1's shield eats the counter-trade. Trade in full rotations.
edits.after: Full kit, but Solar Snare roots from 1000 and Rebuttal reflects the Q behind it — commit only once both are spent.

edits.before: Weave passive autos between every spell. Trade around Rebuttal and bank small HP leads — they compound at 6.
edits.after: Overwhelm stacks build every time she pokes — deny them, hold both E charges, and farm until Hijack lands at 6.

edits.before: Hijack comes online but Mel's R is a reflect tool that is tricky to weaponize directly — both of you are searching for the better trade window rather than either side owning it.
edits.after: Hijack takes Golden Eclipse, which strikes every Overwhelm-marked enemy at any range — you get her own detonation on an 80-second cooldown and she has no dash to leave your E2 chain.

edits.before: Mel's first-item spike (Shadowflame or Luden's) dramatically increases her one-rotation kill threat on a poked Sylas, and Rebuttal still punishes your projectile approach.
edits.after: Riftmaker lands and the W heal starts outpacing her chip; her Shadowflame only one-rotates a Sylas already poked low, so approach on Rebuttal's downtime and fight at full health.

edits.before: Levels 4-5 she still has the edge — her burst grows with levels and Rebuttal stays on a manageable cooldown, so the lane remains hers. Wait for Rebuttal to come off cooldown and visually expire before you commit your E2 hook; one clean E2 stun into Q-W-passive chain is your entire trade pattern and it only works when she cannot immediately reflect your Q. At level 6 the lane becomes contested: you can steal her R, but Mel's ultimate reflects targeted projectiles and her R has a large radius, so its direct value for Sylas is situation-dependent — what matters is denying her the ability to reflect your burst in the all-in. Hook in with E2 on Rebuttal's downtime, burn your rotation into the W heal, and her lack of a hard escape makes the all-in stick.
edits.after: Levels 4-5 she still has the edge — her burst grows with levels and Rebuttal is only a 29-26s cooldown, so the lane remains hers. Wait for Rebuttal to expire before you commit your E2 hook; one clean Abduct into Q-W-passive chain is your entire trade pattern and it only works when she cannot reflect the Q that follows. At level 6 the lane flips: you steal Golden Eclipse, which strikes every enemy carrying Overwhelm at any distance, so it pays best after she has spent the lane stacking you and your team — and stealing it takes the finisher off her side. Hook in with E2 on Rebuttal's downtime, burn your rotation into the W heal, and her lack of a dash makes the all-in stick.
